name: ableton-mind

hlido_opinion.headline: An MCP server for Ableton Live that solves the hard part properly — it re-reads Live's state and diffs against intent instead of assuming the edit worked.
hlido_opinion.body: ableton-mind lets you describe music in natural language and have an assistant build it inside Ableton Live: "128 BPM tech house with a punchy kick, rolling bassline, swung hi-hats" becomes an actual arrangement, read back with a report of what changed. Two design decisions lift this above the usual creative-tool MCP wrapper. First, the verify loop: after every batch of mutations the server re-reads Live's state and diffs it against intent, and tools return `{ ok, verified, diff }` rather than a bare success — that is exactly the discipline most agent-to-application bridges skip, and it is the difference between an assistant that edits your project and one that claims to. Second, the embedded knowledge base: 55+ Live 12 native devices with full parameter schemas (name, range, default, unit), so the model never guesses a parameter name like "Osc 1 Position". Reactive listeners turn Live Object Model property changes into MCP notifications, so the assistant can see the user play or change tempo. Status is stated precisely and modestly — 36 tools today against a stated target of ~180 across 21 LOM domains, 14 recipes, verify loop covering 23/23 mutation tools — and it distinguishes shipped distribution channels from ones pending an admin flow. Requires Ableton Live, so the addressable audience is narrow by design. No adoption figures. Reviewed from the public surface, not run against a real Live install.

tier_rationale: STEADY (72) because the engineering addresses the failure mode that matters for an agent driving a desktop application: a verify loop that re-reads state and returns a diff, plus device parameter schemas so the model works from real names instead of guesses. Precise, non-inflated status reporting (36 of a targeted ~180 tools) adds credibility. Held below VITAL by the absence of adoption evidence, a hard dependency on Ableton Live, and the fact that we could not exercise it against a real install.
what_it_does_well: Verify loop: re-reads Live state after every batch and returns { ok, verified, diff }, not just success
Embedded knowledge base of 55+ Live 12 devices with full parameter schemas — no guessed parameter names
Reactive listeners turn Live Object Model changes into MCP notifications, so the assistant sees user actions
Honest, specific status: 36 tools today against a stated ~180 target, rather than implying completeness
14 declarative recipes across drums, bass, chords, racks, arrangement, mixing and performance
Distinguishes shipped distribution channels from ones still pending an admin publish flow
what_it_fails_at: Hard dependency on Ableton Live — narrow addressable audience by construction
36 of a targeted ~180 tools: most of the Live Object Model surface is not covered yet
No adoption figures, user counts, or third-party validation
Not exercised against a real Live install, so musical output quality is unassessed
Creative-quality outcomes are inherently subjective and cannot be scored from a public surface
best_for: Ableton Live users who want to prototype arrangements conversationally
Producers comfortable with an assistant making verified, diffable changes to a project
Developers building on the Live Object Model who want a documented MCP surface
not_recommended_for: Producers needing full LOM coverage today
Work where an unintended edit to a project file would be costly and un-reviewed

compared_to.note: Same author's TouchDesigner equivalent — same create/verify/preview philosophy applied to a different creative tool.

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: An MCP server first: 36 tools, 5 prompts and 3 MCP resources, plus notifications back to the client. The agent is the operator; the human describes the intent.
